title_card.title: Paris
title_card.note: A city rebuilt in 3D through 2,078 years

cards.title: 2,078 years
cards.years: from the Parisii to the City of Light
cards.note: Illustrative reconstruction · data: Overture Maps, OpenStreetMap contributors, Copernicus

events.title: The Parisii
events.body: A Celtic people live on an island in the Seine, trading along the river

events.title: Rome arrives
events.body: Caesar's general Labienus defeats the Gauls beside the river. The town is burned

events.title: Lutetia
events.body: A Roman town rises on the left bank with a forum, baths and an arena

events.title: Saint Denis
events.body: The first bishop of Paris is put to death on the hill later called Montmartre

events.title: Behind walls
events.body: After raids, the people retreat to the walled island

events.title: An emperor in Paris
events.body: Julian is proclaimed emperor by his soldiers here. The town takes the name Paris

events.title: Attila turns away
events.body: The Huns sweep across Gaul. Led by Genevieve, Parisians stay and pray. Attila passes by

events.title: Clovis
events.body: The King of the Franks makes Paris his capital

events.title: Vikings on the Seine
events.body: Ragnar's fleet sails upriver and sacks the town. A huge ransom sends them away

events.title: The great siege
events.body: Hundreds of longships besiege Paris for nearly a year. The island holds

events.title: Notre-Dame
events.body: Work begins on a new cathedral. It will take nearly two centuries

events.title: A king's wall
events.body: Philip II rings Paris with a wall and builds a fortress: the first Louvre

events.title: Sainte-Chapelle
events.body: Louis IX's chapel of stained glass is consecrated to hold holy relics

events.title: A larger wall
events.body: Charles V builds a new wall around the growing right bank

events.title: The Bastille
events.body: A fortress rises at the city's eastern gate

events.title: The English in Paris
events.body: During the Hundred Years' War, English troops hold the city for 16 years

events.title: St. Bartholomew's Day
events.body: Thousands of Protestants are killed in the streets in a night of religious violence

events.title: Pont Neuf
events.body: The 'New Bridge', now the oldest standing bridge in Paris, opens without houses on it

events.title: Place Royale
events.body: The elegant square later called Place des Vosges is inaugurated

events.title: The court leaves
events.body: Louis XIV moves the royal court to Versailles

events.title: Les Invalides
events.body: A golden dome rises over the home for old soldiers

events.title: The Bastille falls
events.body: Crowds storm the old fortress. The Revolution has begun

events.title: The King is executed
events.body: Louis XVI is guillotined on today's Place de la Concorde

events.title: An emperor crowned
events.body: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor in Notre-Dame

events.title: Allied armies arrive
events.body: Russian and Prussian troops march into Paris. Napoleon abdicates

events.title: The Arc de Triomphe
events.body: Napoleon's victory arch is finished, 30 years after work began

events.title: Barricades
events.body: A revolution ends France's last monarchy

events.title: Haussmann's Paris
events.body: Napoleon III's prefect tears down old quarters for wide boulevards and stone apartment blocks

events.title: The Siege of Paris
events.body: Prussian armies surround the city through a bitter winter

events.title: The Commune
events.body: Fighting ends Paris's revolutionary government. The Tuileries Palace burns

events.title: The Eiffel Tower
events.body: Built for the World's Fair, at 300 m it is the tallest structure on Earth

events.title: The Métro
events.body: The first underground line opens during another World's Fair

events.title: War
events.body: Soldiers march to the front. The Germans are stopped at the Marne

events.title: Armistice
events.body: Paris celebrates the end of the First World War

events.title: Occupation
events.body: German troops enter an almost empty Paris

events.title: Liberation
events.body: Free French and Allied troops free the city. Crowds fill the streets

events.title: May '68
events.body: Students and workers fill the streets. The country nearly stops

events.title: Tour Montparnasse
events.body: Paris's only skyscraper so tall within the city. Taller towers are then banned

events.title: Centre Pompidou
events.body: A museum with its pipes and escalators on the outside

events.title: The Louvre Pyramid
events.body: A glass pyramid becomes the museum's new entrance

events.title: World champions
events.body: France wins the World Cup. Over a million people fill the Champs-Élysées

events.title: Notre-Dame burns
events.body: Fire destroys the roof and the spire. The world watches

events.title: The Olympic Games
events.body: The opening ceremony is held on the Seine, with boats instead of a stadium

events.title: Notre-Dame reopens
events.body: Five years after the fire, the restored cathedral opens its doors

events.title: Paris today
events.body: About 2.1 million people in the city and 12 million in the region
